record.context_brief: non-C2 example for one-pole Green function
record.original_question: Let Omega be a smoothly bounded strictly pseudoconvex domain, and let g_Omega(.,w) be the pluricomplex Green function with one pole w. Since g_Omega is known to lie in C^{1,1}(Omega \ {w}), determine whether there exists an example for which g_Omega fails to be C^2 on Omega minus the pole.

evidence.quote: Question 28 (Blocki). Let Omega be smoothly bounded strictly pseudoconvex domain. It is known that g_Omega in C^{1,1}(Omega \ {w}). Is there an example where g fails to be in C^2(Omega \ {w})?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ ($n \geq 2$) be a smoothly bounded strictly pseudoconvex domain, and fix a point $w \in \Omega$. The pluricomplex Green function with one pole at $w$ is defined by
$$g_\Omega(z,w) = \sup\{u(z) : u \in \mathrm{PSH}(\Omega),\ u < 0,\ u(\zeta) \le \log|\zeta - w| + O(1) \text{ as } \zeta \to w\},$$
where $\mathrm{PSH}(\Omega)$ denotes the cone of plurisubharmonic functions on $\Omega$. It is known that $g_\Omega(\cdot,w) \in C^{1,1}(\overline{\Omega} \setminus \{w\})$.

Question: Does there exist such a domain $\Omega$ and a point $w \in \Omega$ for which $g_\Omega(\cdot,w)$ fails to belong to $C^2(\Omega \setminus \{w\})$?
artifact.status_search_result: The optimal $C^{1,1}$ regularity of the one-pole pluricomplex Green function on smoothly bounded strictly pseudoconvex domains is due to Błocki and Guan. While counterexamples to $C^2$ regularity are known in the multi-pole setting (e.g., the two-pole case on the unit ball of $\mathbb{C}^n$, where the Green function is $C^{1,1}$ but not $C^2$), no such counterexample appears to be known in the one-pole case on a smoothly bounded strictly pseudoconvex domain. The problem is referenced as an open question attributed to Błocki.

status_evidence.title: The C^{1,1} Regularity of the Pluricomplex Green Function (Błocki)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes the C^{1,1} regularity of the one-pole pluricomplex Green function on smoothly bounded strictly pseudoconvex domains.
status_evidence.claim: Best known regularity is C^{1,1}; whether it can fail to be C^2 in the one-pole case is not settled there.

status_evidence.title: The pluricomplex Green function with two poles of the unit ball of C^n
status_evidence.snippet: The Green function with two poles of equal weights on the unit ball is C^{1,1} but not C^2.
status_evidence.claim: A non-C^2 example exists in the multi-pole case, but the one-pole case remains the focus of the question.
